nodes.name: PS — Government Packet Webhook
nodes.notes: Production trigger: receives the ACTUAL government packet PDF as a multipart/form-data upload (file field name: "file"). This is real file bytes handed to n8n by whatever upstream system holds the packet (inbound email-to-webhook, a watched-folder relay, a manual upload form) -- not a URL, not a filename, not JSON. Optional form fields: reference_date (YYYY-MM-DD), live_enrichment (true/false), sync_to_supabase (true/false).

nodes.name: PS — Validate Upload
nodes.notes: Confirms the webhook actually received a binary file under the "file" field before calling the backend. document_downloader.save_uploaded_document() performs the authoritative %PDF magic-byte check server-side -- this is only a fast-fail for a missing/empty upload so a malformed request doesn't waste a backend round trip.

nodes.name: PS — Document Fetch
nodes.notes: Forwards the real uploaded PDF bytes, unmodified, to the PermitSignal backend as a multipart/form-data POST -- POST /pipeline/ingest/file (backend/app/main.py). The backend re-validates the %PDF magic bytes, writes it into data/documents/, then runs the full 7-stage pipeline via pipeline_orchestrator.run_and_save(), including the Supabase upsert when sync_to_supabase=true. No extraction, scoring, or persistence logic runs in n8n.

nodes.name: PS — Validate Document
nodes.notes: Branches on /pipeline/ingest/file's response status. A non-'success' response means either the upload wasn't a real PDF, the pipeline failed, or the backend was unreachable -- routed to the error response path, never silently swallowed.

nodes.name: PS — Run PermitSignal
nodes.notes: Extraction/friction/date/opportunity/identity/enrichment/qualification already ran server-side inside the single /pipeline/ingest/file call above -- this node only surfaces the resulting real counts for the execution log and final response.

nodes.name: PS — Supabase Upsert
nodes.notes: The actual upsert (backend/app/services/lead_repository.upsert_leads, keyed on application_number -- re-ingesting the same packet updates the same rows instead of duplicating them) already ran inside /pipeline/ingest/file when sync_to_supabase=true. This node surfaces its real status (disabled/skipped/synced/error) rather than re-implementing persistence in n8n.

nodes.name: PS — Execution Log
nodes.notes: Summary record for this run. Wire this node's output to whatever execution log you use -- n8n's own execution history already retains the full input/output of every node for traceability (packet -> application_number counts -> processing result -> Supabase status).

string.name: summary
string.value: ={{ 'PermitSignal ingest: ' + $('PS — Run PermitSignal').item.json.applications_count + ' applications, ' + $('PS — Run PermitSignal').item.json.opportunities_count + ' opportunities, supabase_sync=' + $('PS — Supabase Upsert').item.json.supabase_sync_status }}

nodes.name: PS — Success Response
nodes.notes: Structured result returned to the caller. Only fields the backend actually computes today are populated -- this pass does not fabricate new_leads/updated_leads/qualified_leads/follow_up_candidates counts, since change detection (Phase 4) and follow-up routing (Phase 6) are deliberately separate, not-yet-built workflows (see README "Out of scope for this pass").

nodes.name: PS — Respond Success
nodes.notes: Terminal node for a successful intake run -- returns the structured result from PS — Success Response as the webhook's HTTP response.

nodes.name: PS — Error Response
nodes.notes: Reached either when PS — Validate Upload finds no binary file, or PS — Validate Document sees a non-success backend response (invalid PDF, pipeline failure, Supabase failure surfaced via supabase_sync.error, or the backend being unreachable). Errors are surfaced here, never swallowed.

array.name: errors
array.value: ={{ [ $json.detail ?? ( Object.keys($binary || {}).length === 0 ? 'No file uploaded in the "file" field.' : 'PermitSignal processing failed.' ) ] }}

nodes.name: PS — Respond Error
nodes.notes: Terminal node for a failed intake run -- returns a non-2xx structured error so the caller (and n8n's execution history) can see the failure instead of it being silently dropped.
